questions.question_english: A citizen files an RTI application asking for the reasons behind a specific policy decision taken by the Directorate of Education. Which of the following is the legally correct stance for the PIO?
options_english: The PIO must justify the administrative decision and independently draft a complete rationale for the applicant.
The PIO must supply existing records.
The PIO must supply existing records, but need not formulate new reasons.
The PIO must disclose all reasons behind the decision.
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is that the PIO must supply existing records, but need not formulate new reasons. Section 2(f) of the RTI Act mandates Public Information Officers to provide information that is available in recorded form. When an applicant requests reasons behind a policy decision, the officer is obligated to supply existing records, file notings, or documents that contain those reasons. However, the officer is not legally required to draft or generate new justifications that are not already on record.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (c) है। PIO को मौजूदा रिकॉर्ड प्रदान करना होगा, लेकिन नए कारण तैयार करने की आवश्यकता नहीं है। RTI अधिनियम की धारा 2(f) सार्वजनिक सूचना अधिकारियों को रिकॉर्ड में उपलब्ध जानकारी प्रदान करने के लिए बाध्य करती है। जब आवेदक नीति निर्णय के पीछे के कारणों की मांग करता है, तो अधिकारी को मौजूदा रिकॉर्ड, फाइल नोटिंग या दस्तावेज प्रदान करने होंगे जो उन कारणों को शामिल करते हैं। हालांकि, अधिकारी को नए औचित्य तैयार करने की कानूनी आवश्यकता नहीं है जो पहले से रिकॉर्ड में नहीं हैं।
key_facts: Section 2(f) mandates the provision of information in recorded form.
Printed answer key: (c) The PIO must supply existing records.

questions.question_english: Which specific subsection of Section 8(1) exempts information that relates to personal information, the disclosure of which has no relationship to any public activity or interest, or which would cause unwarranted invasion of the privacy of the individual?
options_english: Section 8(1)(d)
Section 8(1)(e)
Section 8(1)(h)
Section 8(1)(j)
questions.explanation_english: Section 8(1)(j) of the Right to Information Act specifically deals with personal information exemptions. It protects personal information from disclosure if it has no relationship to any public activity or interest, or if it would cause an unwarranted invasion of individual privacy, unless the competent authority determines that larger public interest justifies such disclosure.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। धारा 8(1)(j) सूचना के अधिकार अधिनियम में व्यक्तिगत जानकारी की छूट से संबंधित है। यह व्यक्तिगत जानकारी को प्रकटीकरण से बचाता है यदि इसका किसी सार्वजनिक गतिविधि या हित से कोई संबंध नहीं है, या यदि यह व्यक्ति की गोपनीयता में अनावश्यक हस्तक्षेप का कारण बनता है, जब तक कि सक्षम प्राधिकारी यह निर्धारित न करे कि बड़ा सार्वजनिक हित ऐसे प्रकटीकरण को उचित ठहराता है।
key_facts: Section 8(1)(j) exempts personal information from disclosure.
Printed answer key: (d) Section 8(1)(j)

questions.question_english: What happens when an RTI application asks a hypothetical question or seeks the “opinion” or “advice” of the PIO on a matter where no such recorded opinion exists in the files?
options_english: The PIO is required to generate the opinion after formal consultation with the Head of Department.

questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is option d. The Right to Information Act covers information that is held in recorded form by a public authority. A Public Information Officer is required to supply existing records and data, but is under no legal obligation to generate fresh opinions, create hypothetical answers, or provide legal advice that does not exist in recorded official files.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम उस जानकारी को कवर करता है जो सार्वजनिक प्राधिकरण द्वारा रिकॉर्डेड रूप में रखी जाती है। एक जन सूचना अधिकारी को मौजूदा रिकॉर्ड और डेटा प्रदान करने की आवश्यकता होती है, लेकिन उसे नई राय उत्पन्न करने, काल्पनिक उत्तर बनाने, या ऐसी कानूनी सलाह देने के लिए कोई कानूनी बाध्यता नहीं होती जो आधिकारिक फाइलों में मौजूद नहीं है।

questions.question_english: What is the consequence if the First Appellate Authority (FAA) fails to pass an order within the maximum prescribed time limit of 45 days?

questions.explanation_english: When the First Appellate Authority fails to issue an order within the statutory limit of thirty or forty-five days, the appeal remains unresolved. questions.question_english: According to Section 20(2) of the RTI Act, apart from imposing a financial penalty, what other action can the Information Commission recommend against an erring PIO?

questions.explanation_english: Section 20(2) empowers Information Commissions to recommend disciplinary action against defaulting Public Information Officers. questions.explanation_english: The Freedom of Information Act, 2002 was enacted but never brought into force, later being replaced by the RTI Act 2005. The legislative evolution of information rights in India saw the passage of the Freedom of Information Act, 2002. However, this earlier statute was never formally brought into force due to statutory limitations and administrative delays. It was subsequently repealed and replaced by the comprehensive Right to Information Act, 2005, establishing a stronger regulatory framework nationwide.

questions.question_english: A PIO rejects an RTI application stating that compiling the requested information would disproportionately divert the resources of the school. The PIO relies on Section 7(9). Is the PIO’s outright rejection legally sound?
options_english: Yes, Section 7(9) provides an absolute statutory exemption whenever compilation diverts administrative resources.
No, Section 7(9) is not an exemption; it only allows providing information in another format.

questions.explanation_english: Section 7(9) states that information shall ordinarily be provided in the requested format unless doing so would disproportionately divert public authority resources. This provision regulates the mode or format of providing information and does not create an independent statutory exemption ground for outright rejection of an information application under the Act.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। धारा 7(9) कहती है कि जानकारी सामान्यतः अनुरोधित प्रारूप में प्रदान की जानी चाहिए जब तक कि ऐसा करना सार्वजनिक प्राधिकरण के संसाधनों को असमान रूप से विकसित नहीं करता। यह प्रावधान जानकारी प्रदान करने के तरीके या प्रारूप को नियंत्रित करता है और अधिनियम के तहत सूचना आवेदन के सीधे अस्वीकार के लिए स्वतंत्र वैधानिक छूट का आधार नहीं बनाता।
